tone_statements.translation: For the transcription we follow the writing norm proposed by SEP-INALI (2014), which includes 24 consonants [...], 14 vowels, 9 oral (...) and 5 nasal (...), and 3 tones (v́ [high], v [low], vv [rising]). [fn.1:] Although we follow the SEP-INALI (2014) norm, the rising tone, which the norm marks by doubling the tone-bearing vowel, is represented here with the caron diacritic.

audit.reasoning: Quote confirmed verbatim at Blight & Pike 1976:56 section 8 in the text we hold layer. The deciding source is the sole dedicated phonology of the variety (IJAL, SIL fieldworkers), and both the newer specialist's open-access 2021 paper (downloaded now, p.6: tonic syllable = usually first syllable of lexical roots) and the held Sierra Otomi grammar (Voigtlander & Echegoyen 1979:23-24: stress always on first syllable of the root, proclitics unstressed, alternating rhythm) agree with stem-initial primary stress plus alternating secondaries, i.e. the coded 10/100/1010/10100 pattern. No grammar, dissertation or instrumental study of Tenango Otomi stress exists to supersede it; the one unheld item (IJAL 2021, paywalled) is about grammatical tone and unlikely to change the classification. One note for the catalog, not a reclassify: all three sources locate primary stress on the first syllable of the stem/root

sources.quote: 'La lengua tiene tres tonemas distintos: alto (A), bajo (B) y ascendente (C), contrastivos (léxica y gramaticalmente) en sílaba tónica (usualmente la primera sílaba de las raíces léxicas); los tonos A y B también son contrastivos en algunos clíticos.'
